key_insight: The paper proposes CMA-AL, a six-level autonomy framework that defines how computational materials systems can progress from scripted simulation execution to self-extending discovery agents.
engineering_relevance: It gives researchers and platform builders a shared benchmark for designing, comparing, and scaling agentic AI workflows in materials simulation and discovery.
method: Defines six autonomy levels: scripted executor, LLM-assisted operator, adaptive explorer, experiment-ready modeler, agentic digital twin, and self-extending intelligence.
Maps emerging agentic materials systems onto the taxonomy to assess current maturity and gaps.
Identifies technical and scientific challenges needed to move toward higher autonomy.
evidence_signal: This is a perspective paper that synthesizes the field and proposes a conceptual framework; the abstract does not report new experimental data or benchmark results.
watch_item: The framework is conceptual, so practical adoption will depend on clear operational criteria and reliable evaluation metrics for autonomy across diverse materials workflows.
paper_title: From Automated Simulation to Autonomous Discovery: A Hierarchical Framework for Agentic Computational Materials Science
